themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree this is leadership rotation, not a broad top — but index calm overstates breadth because the index is carried by a narrowing set of weights. The divergence is real and worth tracking precisely because credit can flip: if SLOOS tightens or HY OAS widens, the same concentration turns rotation into unwind.

themes.counterRead: If these were clean sentiment dislocations, the promotion engine would have promoted at least one to conviction. Zero conviction promotions plus a live earnings-miss headline inside the same screened universe says the SENTIMENT_DRIVEN tag cannot by itself separate a sentiment cut from a guidance break. Treat the pile-up as a verification queue, name by name, not a basket buy.

themes.counterRead: Narrative and data agree on the squeeze, and the split inside the data is the point: restrictive nominal rates with tight spreads and contained breakevens is a valuation headwind for small caps and long-duration equity, not a credit event. Cash-flow-today names keep the bid until either the 10-year breaks or spreads crack — the Oct 27-28 FOMC is the next dated hinge.
themes.dataAnchor: The curve prices restriction: DGS10 at 5.27%, DGS30 at 5.64%, real 10-year at 2.91%, 2s10s at +0.43 and DFF at 3.88%. The damage is visible exactly where duration bites: IWM -1.7% today, -5.89% over one month and -6.8% over three months, while SPY is +0.67% over one month and QQQ +4.78%. themes.label: 5.27% Ten-Year: Restriction Lands on Small Caps, Not Credit
